sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the rankings of the parties would be henceforth referred to as per their rankings before the Trial Court.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
It is the case of the prosecution that P.W.1 lodged a complaint stating that the victim is her daughter.
She was residing in Madikeri along with her daughter.
Her daughter was NC: 2024:KHC:48141-DB aged about 15 years and she was studying in 10th standard.
It is further stated in the complaint that her daughter had gone out of the house on 06.11.2018 and thereafter, on 09.11.2018, she came back to her house.
When it was questioned by P.W.1, she was told that the victim had accompanied accused No.2 and went to his grandfather's house.
4. It is further stated that the victim was suffering from some medical issues like suffering from weakness, giddiness etc.
She was taken to the hospital for treatment.
She had not recovered, despite some medications.
In the meantime, P.W.1 and her sister noticed that the victim seems to be pregnant.
When P.W.1 and her sister questioned about the pregnancy, it was informed that accused No.1-Shashi Kumar had taken her to the bakery where he was working and said to have committed sexual assault.

Further, it was also told that when accused No.2 had taken the victim to his grandfather's house, he also committed sexual assault.
5.
P.W.1 after hearing the matter from the victim, took the victim to the hospital for medical examination.
The doctor confirmed that she was pregnant.

After hearing the said NC:
2024:KHC:48141-DB news, P.W.1 informed the same to accused No.2.
He promised P.W.1 that he would marry the victim and took her along with him and kept her in his house for 15 days.
On 07.01.2019, when the victim informed P.W.1 regarding her health issues, she was brought back to Madikeri and she had been subjected for medical examination.
The doctor opined that the victim was 21 weeks pregnant.
Hence, a complaint came to be registered against accused Nos.1 and 2.
After conducting the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
6. To prove the case of the prosecution, the prosecution has examined 20 witnesses as P.Ws.1 to 20 and got marked 27 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.27.
The Trial Court after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, recorded the conviction for the above said offences.
Hence, these appeals.

7. Heard Sri. C.Parameshwarappa, learned counsel for the appellant in Crl.A.No.1482/2019,
Sri.Lethif B, learned counsel for the appellant in Crl.A.No.428/2020, Sri. Vijaykumar Majage,
learned SPP-II for respondent No.1-State and Sri. NC: 2024:KHC:48141-DB Tejas, learned Amicus Ranjith Kumar P @ Ranjith vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52078618/
4 Curiae for respondent No.2 in both the appeals.
8.

entities.text: Amicus Ranjith Kumar P @ Ranjith vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the submission of learned counsel for accused No.1 that the judgment of conviction and order on sentence passed by the Trial Court is erroneous and not proper.
It is further submitted that the judgment contains some findings which are contrary to the evidence on record.
Therefore, the same may be set aside.

9. It is further submitted that, except the evidence of P.W.17-victim, none of the witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution regarding friendship or existence of any relationship between the victim and accused No.1.
It is a fact that there were two persons named in the FIR including accused No.1.
Even though, the victim made certain allegations about sexual assault, that may not be sufficient to hold him guilty for the aforesaid offences.

10. It is further submitted that though the Investigating Officer stated to have collected the blood samples of all the three persons including the foetus for DNA examination, however, the prosecution has not produced the report from NC: 2024:KHC:48141-DB FSL.

In the absence of a concrete report to substantiate that accused No.1 has committed sexual assault, arriving at a conclusion that accused No.1 committed sexual assault is not proper and the Trial Court has lost sight of the facts and circumstances of the case and recorded the conviction which is liable to be set aside.
Making such submissions, the learned counsel for accused No.1 prays to allow the appeal.

11. Similarly, the learned counsel for accused No.2 also vehemently controverted the findings recorded by the Trial Court relating to the conviction of accused No.2 and he submitted that the complaint averments discloses that accused No.1 is the reason for the pregnancy of the victim and further the said victim had stated before the Magistrate that accused No.1 was responsible for her pregnancy.
Even in the evidence of P.Ws.1 and 17, the said fact has been reiterated by them.
12. It is further submitted that the accused No.2 was working as a carpenter in the school where the victim was studying in the X standard.
Both have acquainted with each other.

As P.W.1 being a mother of P.W.17 had narrated the incident of pregnancy of the victim to accused No.2, he NC:
2024:KHC:48141-DB intended to marry her and took her along with him.
Since the victim had not completed the age of 18 years, he brought her back to the house of P.W.1 and assured her that he would marry her after attaining the age of marriage.
However, P.W.1 with an ulterior motive, filed a false case against him in order to use the coercive method for the marriage.
13. It is further submitted that the prosecution has not produced any DNA report to show that accused No.2 was responsible for either pregnancy or sexual assault.
Such being the fact, the conviction ought not to have been recorded based on the evidence of sole prosecutrix without corroboration.
Since the Trial Court has committed an error, the appeal needs to be allowed.
Making such submissions, the learned counsel for accused No.2 prays to allow the appeal.
14. Per contra, learned SPP-II vehemently justified the judgment of conviction passed by the Trial Court and he further submitted that the victim was a school-going child, aged about 15 years.
She was staying along with her mother and aunt.

While she was going to school, she had to cross the Ranjith Kumar P @ Ranjith vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52078618/
5 bakery which was situated in the same road.

sentences.text: Accused No.1 has - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:48141-DB developed friendship with the victim and induced her that he would marry her and took her to the bakery and committed sexual assault.
Further, he threatened her that he would publish her photographs to her mother and others.
In such a way, he was sexually assaulting the victim.

15. It is further submitted that, accused No.2 was working as a carpenter where the victim was studying and he induced the victim that he would take care of her and also assuring her that he would marry her, initially took her to the house of his grandfather.
After three days, he brought her back to her house.
After she came back to her home, it was diagnosed that she was pregnant.
The fact of the said pregnancy was made known to accused No.2 by P.W.1.
Then, again he took her to his grandfather's house and kept her for fifteen days and brought her back to her house.
During the stay, accused No.2 stated to have committed sexual assault on the victim.
Therefore, the prosecution has made out a case against accused Nos.1 and 2.
The Trial Court rightly recorded the conviction.
The findings recorded by the Trial Court are appropriate and proper.
Interference with the said findings - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:48141-DB may not be necessary.
Making such submissions, the leaned SPP-II prays to dismiss the appeals.

16. Learned Amicus Curiae for respondent No.2 in both appeals has adopted the arguments of the learned High Court Government Pleader and prays to upheld the judgment of conviction and order on sentence passed by the Trial Court.

17. After having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the findings of the Trial Court in recording the conviction, it is appropriate to refer the evidence of all the witnesses for the purpose of re-appreciation.

18. P.W.1 being the mother of the victim has deposed that her daughter was studying in X standard as on the date when she was diagnosed as pregnant and further, she deposed that accused No.1 was responsible for the said pregnancy and accused No.2 also held responsible for sexual assault committed against the minor girl.
She identified her complaint which is marked as Ex.P.1.
Despite cross-examination, she supported the case of the prosecution and she was consistent that accused No.1 was responsible for the pregnancy of her minor daughter.

6 19.

sentences.text: P.W.2 is the elder sister of P.W.1 and she also reiterated the fact that the accused No.1 was responsible for the pregnancy of the victim.
She was treated as hostile and cross-examined by the prosecution.
She admitted certain facts in the cross-examination.
Since she is a hearsay witness, her evidence in respect of the alleged incident may be taken into consideration as a corroborative piece of evidence.
20. P.W.3 has been examined to ascertain as to whether accused No.2 had taken the victim to his house or not.
She being a neighbour, has not supported the case of the prosecution.
Therefore, she has been treated as hostile and conducted cross-examination.
However, nothing has been elicited from her.
21. P.W.4 is also examined for the similar purpose as that of P.W.3.
He also not supported the case of the prosecution.
22. P.W.5 is the witness to Ex.P.3, supported the case of the prosecution.
P.W.6 is also examined for the purpose of confronting the document which is marked as Ex.P.3 and he supported the case of the prosecution.
24. P.W.7 was supposed to be the witness to Ex.P.4 which is known as spot mahazar.
He has not supported the case of the prosecution.

25. P.W.8 is also the same as that of P.W.7 and not supported the case of the prosecution.
26.
P.W.9 was working as PDO, Channayanakote Grama Panchayath.

He said to have given assessment of the house as per Ex.P.8.
27.
P.W.10 was working as a woman PSI, said to have registered a case in Cr.No.1/2019 and the said FIR is marked as Ex.P.9.
28 . P.W.11 was working as a medical officer said to have conducted the medical examination of accused No.2 and submitted the report as per Ex.P.11.
P.W.12 is said to have issued the residential certificate of grandfather's house of accused No.2 situated at Duddagallu village as per Ex.

7 30.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: P.W.13 was working as Head Constable at Madikeri Women police station.

He said to have arrested accused No.1 on 10.01.2019.
31.
P.W.14 was deputed to arrest accused No.2.

Accordingly, he arrested him on 10.01.2019 around 10.00 a.m.
32.
P.W.15 was working as incharge Head Master, said to have issued the study certificate of the victim as per Ex.P.16.
33. P.W.16 was working as a Gynaecologist at Kodagu District Hospital.

She stated to have conducted medical examination of the victim and submitted the report as per Ex.P.2.
34.
P.W.17 is the victim and she has supported the case of the prosecution.
She was consistent that accused No.1 is responsible for her pregnancy and also stated that accused No.2 had committed sexual assault on her.
P.W.18 is said to have issued the certificate in respect of the rented house of P.W.1 and the same has been marked as Ex.P.26.
36. P.W.19 was supposed to be the witness to the Ex.P.5 which is considered as spot mahazar.
As per the said mahazar, the victim had shown the place where she was staying along with accused No.2.
However, he has not supported the case of the prosecution.
37. P.W.20 was working as a Circle Inspector, Madikeri police station, stated to have conducted investigation and submitted the charge sheet.
38. On careful reading of evidence of all the witnesses, it is relevant to refer the evidence of P.W.1, 2 and 17 who are the material witnesses of the case.
They deposed about the sexual assault on the victim and about the incident.
According to the evidence of P.W.17, she was going to school on every day.
While she was going to school, she had to cross the bakery where accused No.1 was working in the said bakery.
It is stated that both accused No.1 and victim gradually developed friendship and thereafter, he proposed her for - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:48141-DB marriage.
In the said context, he took her to his bakery where he was working and said to have committed sexual assault.
According to her, she was blackmailed by accused No.1 that he would show her nude photos to her mother and others.
In that context, he said to have been committing sexual assault on several occasions.
Thereafter, he completely ignored her.

Ranjith Kumar P @ Ranjith vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52078618/
8 39.

entities.text: Ranjith Kumar P @ Ranjith vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: P.W.17 further deposed that again, she developed intimacy with accused No.2 who was working as a carpenter in her school.
It is stated that, she went along with him and stayed in the grandfather's house of accused No.2 for three days and came back to her house.
Later, she was diagnosed as pregnant and again, she was taken to the house of accused No.2 and accused No.2 kept her for fifteen days and brought her back to her house.
40. According to P.W.17, accused No.1 was responsible for her pregnancy.

The prosecution even though collected blood samples of all the three persons including the foetus for the purpose of conducting the DNA examination, however, no report was produced for the purpose of clarification.
On careful reading of evidence of P.W.17, it appears from her evidence that initially she developed friendship with accused No.1 and he committed sexual assault on her and he ignored her.
Thereafter, she developed friendship with accused No.2.
He took her to his grandfather's house and there he committed sexual assault.
The fact of sexual assault was not disclosed by the victim to her mother and aunt until her pregnancy was known to them.
Of course, the sexual assault committed against a minor requires to be seen with utmost care and caution.
No doubt, the law is settled on the said principle and that is why the Parliamentarians enacted the POCSO Act, 2012 in order to regulate the exploitation, sexual assault against the minor girls.
42. The evidence of P.W.17 regarding sexual assault committed by accused Nos.1 and 2 cannot be accepted for the reason that, except her evidence, there is no corroboration or medical evidence.
In the absence of independent corroboration, either oral or documentary, it is hard to believe the evidence of P.W.17.
It is needless to say that the Investigating Officer has not collected the DNA Report and the prosecution has not made any efforts to secure and get it marked.
Therefore, I am of the - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:48141-DB considered opinion that the Trial Court has committed an error in recording the conviction of the accused.

43. In the light of the observations made above, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeals are allowed.
ii) The judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 07.08.2019 passed in Spl.C.No.14/2019 by the learned Prl. Sessions Judge, Kodagu at Madikeri is hereby set aside.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is a fact that there were two persons named in the FIR including accused No.1.
Even though, the victim made certain allegations about sexual assault, that may not be sufficient to hold him guilty for the aforesaid offences.
Since the victim had not completed the age of 18 years, he brought her back to the house of P.W.1 and assured her that he would marry her after attaining the age of marriage.
However, P.W.1 with an ulterior motive, filed a false case against him in order to use the coercive method for the marriage.
Such being the fact, the conviction ought not to have been recorded based on the evidence of sole prosecutrix without corroboration.
